name: Corn smut
symptoms: general: Tumor-like galls on plant tissues Swollen kernels or plant organs Black powdery spores inside galls leaves: Small galls on leaf veins or blades stems: Large galls on stalks or nodes ears: Kernels replaced by swollen galls Galls turn black and rupture releasing spores
description: Corn smut is a fungal disease of maize that produces tumor-like galls on different parts of the plant. These galls contain masses of dark spores and can significantly reduce yield. In Mexico, immature galls are considered a culinary delicacy known as huitlacoche.
management: cultural: Use resistant maize varieties Practice crop rotation Remove infected plant debris Avoid mechanical injury to plants Manage nitrogen fertilization chemical: Fungicides are generally ineffective for controlling corn smut
